chunks: Via his chain to Abdallah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari who said:

I asked Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri (may Allah be pleased with him): Have you seen the Master of this Order (peace be upon him)? He said: Yes. My last meeting with him was at the Sanctified House of Allah [the Ka'ba], and he was saying: 'O Allah, fulfill for me what You promised me.' Muhammad ibn Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him and be pleased with him) said: I also saw him (may Allah's prayers be upon him) clinging to the coverings of the Ka'ba at the Mustajar [place of refuge] while he was saying: 'O Allah, take revenge for me from Your enemies.'

key_terms.الْمُسْتَجَارِ: The place of refuge (a specific area near the Ka'ba)
key_terms.بَيْتِ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامِ: The Sanctified House of Allah (the Ka'ba)
key_terms.صَاحِبَ الْأَمْرِ: Master of the Order (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say when he was at the Ka'ba according to Muhammad ibn Uthman?
ai.summary: This narration from Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri, one of the Four Deputies of the Hidden Imam, highlights the Imam's active supplication at the Ka'ba during the Major Occultation, emphasizing his dual role as both the Awaited Savior and the intercessor seeking divine vengeance against oppressors. The specific mention of 'clinging to the coverings of the Ka'ba' (Mustajar) underscores the physical and spiritual proximity of the Imam to the House of God, reinforcing the Shia belief in his continuous presence and vigilance. This event serves as a foundational proof for the Imam's visibility and agency even in the later stages of the Occultation, bridging the gap between the era of the Four Deputies and the General Occultation.
